context.note: Queue task 355, GH#700, stage S6. Design produced on branch feature/WF02-REQ182-20260829 (already checked out). Design covers the route/controller layer only, atop REQ-181's already-shipped lib/letflow/webhooks.ex (create/2, list/1, update/3, delete/2 -- note the real function is update/3, not update/2 as REQ-182's own requirement text loosely says; the design uses the real signature throughout) and lib/letflow/webhooks/subscription.ex. lib/letflow/routers/dlq.ex (REQ-178) was used as the closest precedent for the AuthorizedRouter idiom, the cross-tenant-404 mechanism, and the hand-built JSON allowlist. lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex was read in full for the real WebhooksManage/WebhookSubscriptionsManage permission mapping: the design found that endpoint_policy_key/2 already has GET/POST '/webhooks/subscriptions' and DELETE '/webhooks/subscriptions/:id' clauses (both -> :WebhookSubscriptionsManage -> :WebhooksManage), but is MISSING a PATCH '/webhooks/subscriptions/:id' clause -- the design specifies adding exactly that one clause as in-scope for this requirement (design section 4.3). Verified role_allows?/2's real clauses: only PLATFORM_ADMIN (catch-all) and PROCESS_OPERATOR (explicit) hold :WebhooksManage; PROCESS_DESIGNER/TASK_WORKER/AGENT_RUNNER do not.

task.description: Validate lib/letflow/design/req182-webhooks-routes.md against REQ-182's full acceptance criteria (docs/requirements.yaml#REQ-182). Confirm: (1) every acceptance criterion maps to a concrete, unambiguous design element -- no TBD; (2) the design contains no fenced code block reproducing real or near-real .ex file content (function bodies/composed expressions) -- signatures, @spec/@type declarations, and plain data tables only; (3) the route-to-context-function param mapping (section 3) is faithful to lib/letflow/webhooks.ex's real create/2, list/1, update/3, delete/2 @specs as they actually exist on disk today; (4) the permission-mapping claims in section 4 (including the missing-PATCH-clause finding) are independently re-verified against lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex's real, current clauses, not merely trusted from this handoff's own note; (5) the JSON allowlist (section 5) never emits secret_hash or an unscoped hmac_secret_once, and the create-response hmac_secret_once splice is confined to the one documented branch.
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions with no secret supplied returns a 2xx response whose body includes hmac_secret_once carrying the plaintext secret exactly once; a subsequent GET/list of the same subscription never includes the plaintext secret or an hmac_secret_once field at all -- two explicit tests
PATCH /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions/:id accepts {status: "PAUSED"} and, separately, {is_active: false}, and both result in a subscription that subsequently reads back as PAUSED via GET/list

every subscription route requires the WebhooksManage permission from REQ-069's matrix -- a caller lacking it receives 403, and a caller from a different tenant naming a real subscription id belonging to tenant A receives 404, never 403
GET /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions returns {items: [...]} with each item's target_url, event_types, status and created_at present, matching webhooksApi.list's consumer shape
DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions/:id removes the subscription such that a subsequent list no longer includes it, and a second DELETE of the same id returns 404 rather than a duplicate success

the route module's moduledoc states explicitly that R-Co's webhooks.zig was not inspected in this batch (unreachable from the drafting environment) and that web/src/api/dlq.ts / web/src/types/api.ts were the binding contract instead
the design contains no fenced code block reproducing real or near-real .ex file content (function bodies/composed expressions) -- signatures, @spec/@type declarations, and plain data tables only

result.summary: Independently re-verified all flagged claims against the real files (not the handoff's own note). (1) endpoint_policy_key/2 in lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex (lines 289-297) has GET/POST '/webhooks/subscriptions', GET '/webhooks/subscriptions/:id/deliveries', and DELETE '/webhooks/subscriptions/:id' clauses, all -> :WebhookSubscriptionsManage, and genuinely lacks a PATCH '/webhooks/subscriptions/:id' clause -- the design's section 4.3 gap-finding and proposed one-clause fix are correct and correctly scoped (no new permission atom, no new role_allows?/2 clause). (2) role_allows?/2 confirmed: PLATFORM_ADMIN catch-all (line 443) and PROCESS_OPERATOR's explicit list including :WebhooksManage (line 469) are the only two holders; PROCESS_DESIGNER (445-454) and TASK_WORKER (472-473) omit it, AGENT_RUNNER is always false (475). (3) lib/letflow/webhooks.ex's real signatures match the design's section 3/6 tables exactly: create/2 -> {:ok, %{subscription:, hmac_secret_once:}} | {:error, Ecto.Changeset.t()}; list/1 -> {:ok, [Subscription.t()]} only; update/3 -> 5-variant union ({:ok,_}, :invalid_id, :not_found, :invalid_status, changeset error), all handled in section 3.3; delete/2 -> 3-variant union, all handled in section 3.4. lib/letflow/webhooks/subscription.ex confirms no hmac_secret_once struct field and secret_hash as the only secret-shaped column, supporting the section 5 allowlist claims. (4) grep for triple-backtick fences in the design file returned zero matches -- no implementation code present, only prose, tables, and named signatures. All 7 acceptance criteria map to concrete design elements with no TBD/deferral language. Approved for implementation.
